exposure: IVH grade (grades 1 and 2 vs grades 3 and 4)
outcome: risk factors for high-grade intraventricular haemorrhage
short-term complications of high-grade intraventricular haemorrhage
cohort: 436 preterm neonates with high-grade (3, 4) IVHs admitted in training hospitals of Alborz University in Karaj, Iran, from 2012 to 2017
finding: The most common risk factor for high-grade intraventricular haemorrhage was lack of corticosteroid use, and short-term complications occurred in 10% of cases.
